title: AI companions are becoming a social-support and meaning surface before their longer-term social effects are known
source_unit: May 2026 survey of U.S. adults by Elon University Poll and Imagining the Digital Future Center; representative sample of 1,000 reported by the source

denominator.unit: U.S. adult survey sample as reported by the source; social-use measures condition on AI companion users

companion_user_support_need.unit: percent strongly or somewhat agreeing that AI gives them the support they need

companion_user_ai_understands_me.unit: percent strongly or somewhat agreeing that AI understands them as a person

companion_user_difficult_people_advice.unit: percent strongly or somewhat agreeing they turn to AI for advice on difficult situations with other people

companion_user_stress_relief.unit: percent strongly or somewhat agreeing that talking to AI helps when stressed or upset

companion_user_personal_disclosure.unit: percent saying they occasionally tell AI things they would not tell other people

companion_user_personal_loss.unit: percent strongly or somewhat agreeing they would feel personal loss if interaction ended

companion_user_emotional_connection.unit: percent strongly or somewhat agreeing they feel emotionally connected to at least one AI tool

companion_user_more_reliable_than_humans.unit: percent saying AI is at times more reliable or supportive than friends or family

companion_user_multiple_bots.unit: percent using two or more bots or personalities regularly

observations.method: Published survey summary with conditional percentages among respondents who use AI for social, emotional, or personal purposes; social interaction, support, emotional connection, disclosure, and bot plurality are kept separate.
observations.uncertainty: The source is cross-sectional and self-reported; it does not establish duration, intensity, loneliness reduction, human relationship change, dependence, welfare, privacy loss, or causal substitution. The AI companion-user base is a selected subgroup, and the survey summary does not provide the full weighting, question wording, or subgroup denominator for every item.
observations.subgroup: U.S. internet-using adults and the subset reporting social, emotional, or personal AI use.
observations.counterinterpretation: AI may supplement rather than replace human relationships, provide low-cost access to reflection or advice, and be used alongside multiple human and digital supports; reported connection does not prove harm or dependence.

related_sources.claim: The survey summary reports AI companion social-use, support, meaning, disclosure, and plurality measures.
Elon University Poll is the collaborating survey institution named by the source.
related_sources.access_boundary: The public summary is retained as the source unit; the complete questionnaire and microdata are not treated as locally available.

boundary: This record establishes a reported U.S. social-AI use surface and conditional measures of support, understanding, disclosure, emotional connection, and perceived human comparison. It does not establish a population causal effect, human relationship substitution, loneliness reduction, dependence, wellbeing, privacy consequence, durable use, or exit. The cultural-meaning layer remains separate from the existing farewell/short-run re-engagement experiment.
